To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a) a 3D finite element based analysis and design tool for D regions can be used by the less experienced finite element user; b) the tool can be applied for the analysis and/or design of 3 D D regions with a good accuracy; c) a strut and tie based approach is proposed for the analysis and simplified design of four pile cap with rectangular geometry.

a simple finite element based approach can be developed for the analysis and rational design of D regions in 3D; a 3D nonlinear concrete constitutive model based only on the uniaxal compressive strength is sufficient to obtain realistic response predictions; a strut and tie based analysis and design procedure can be formulated to predict the ultimate strength and mode of failure of four pile caps.

the use of finite elements for the analysis and/or design of 3d reinforced concrete D regions is a promising approach that can be implemented in a user friendly manner, that the use of a simple orthotropic concrete model is sufficient to obtain accurate results for the analysis and that the use of this model in the context of a strut and tie based approach is a rational way to obtain reliable results.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a finite element based tool for the analysis and the design of 3d reinforced concrete elements and structures with D regions, which is based on simple constitutive laws.
the analysis and design in practice of D regions by means of a 3D nonlinear FE tool.
the development of a finite element based analysis tool for 3D D region elements and with the proposal of a strut and tie based approach for the design of rectangular four pile caps.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the tool presented in this thesis is a valuable aid to deal with the analysis and design 3D D region elements.
the finite element method is not a tool to replace current design methods but rather a tool which complements them and permits to deal with complex geometries.
the tool developed in this thesis is a powerful and versatile tool to deal with the analysis and design problems associated with 3D reinforced and prestressed concrete elements.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the finite element based tool developed in this thesis can be used for the analysis and rational design of 3 D reinforced concrete elements.
the proposed method is able to provide rational solutions to the design of four pile cap D regions.
the developed finite element tool can be a useful aid in the analysis and design for D regions, especially for the less experienced finite element user.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of finite elements for the analysis and the design of 3d D regions is a powerful tool that permits to obtain more rational solutions.
a simple finite element tool based on a relatively simple constitutive model can be used to obtain realistic predictions of the strength and failure mode of 3D RC structures.
finite element based approaches can facilitate a better design of 3 D regions and that simple concrete constitutive models can be adopted to this purpose.
